scope.topic: The mental health system of systems in North Alabama: WellStone's service area (Madison and Cullman counties in depth; the fifteen-county Huntsville crisis-center catchment in outline), as a regional edition of the Alabama Mental Health Systems Report.
scope.question: What does the mental health system of systems look like in WellStone's service area in October 2026 (who decides, who pays, what exists, who delivers it, who is reached and who is missed) in Madison and Cullman counties, and how does the wider fifteen-county crisis catchment depend on it?

known_gaps: The search tool returns a page of results without a total, so hit counts are not available; every query is listed with what it was for.
390 page reads failed across the two sweeps, most refused by a site's request limit or its robots rule. None was worked around; the principal ones are in the open items.

Most wellstone.com pages refused the page reader; WellStone's own description of its programs, locations and board is therefore under-read, and the report leans on documents WellStone filed with the state, federal award records and the press.

Sources were read through an automated page reader that returns extracts. Passages are as it returned them; paraphrases are flagged, and tables it returned inconsistently are listed under 'Needs a human eye'.

Census, CDC, HRSA and County Health Rankings data sites are not reachable from the research environment. County figures come from the statewide pack's checked table. Tract-level map data was retrieved on 4 October 2026 through the browser on the builder's own computer and checked against checksums computed in the browser (geo/raw/checks.md). Tract boundaries are not in the pack: the app fetches the Census Bureau's boundary file when it is built.

Service locations on the map were placed by geocoding the addresses printed in the sources. Two could not be placed, and WellStone's Huntsville campus is placed from a federal treatment locator whose two records for the address disagree; geo/NOTES.md lists every such case.

synthesis.excerpt: None of this is unusual for a state that built its regional lines one program at a time, but it has a practical consequence. The fifteen counties are not a unit in any of the other regional schemes re

It would be easy to stop there, with a prosperous metro county and a struggling rural one. The city figures spoil that picture. Inside Madison County, median household income is $134,655 in the city o

The board has eighteen members. Six are appointed by the City of Huntsville, six by the Madison County Commission, three by the City of Cullman and three by the Cullman County Commission [1]. The Cull

Representation has not followed the catchment. The board that governs a fifteen-county crisis center is appointed by four governments in two counties [1] [3]. No public document describes how the othe

The plan's goals are the organization's, and the needs are the community's. WellStone's plan names housing, medication funding, nursing and commitment stabilization as needs and priorities, and then s

One court has built a program; neither publishes its numbers. Madison County's outpatient commitment program is known mainly through press reports and a federal award record, and Cullman's court publi
Federal grants are the exception, because the federal government publishes them. The Department of Health and Human Services' grants database shows three awards to WellStone between fiscal years 2021

Any per-person figure for the region has to be computed, because nobody publishes one, and the results below are this report's arithmetic. Huntsville's FY2026 allotment to WellStone after amendment, $

Four years without a public return. The region's principal provider has no Form 990 data on the public record after FY2021, a period in which it opened a crisis center, a pediatric unit and a detox pr

Grant-built programs reach the end of their grants. The assisted outpatient treatment award ran to 30 July 2026 and the CCBHC implementation grant to 29 September 2026 [37] [39]. Whether Medicaid's ne
Capital was raised in public; operating support is settled in budget lines that are hard to find. Of five local governments, one published an amount for FY2026 that a reader could open [98].

Settlement money has gone to different places in each county. Huntsville funded homelessness services, a hospital foundation and WellStone; Cullman funded a free clinic, a drug court and a recovery no

The pressure has moved downstream. Access to a first appointment improved and crisis admissions more than tripled, while the things WellStone's plan and the probate court both ask for are what follows

Cullman has the first half of a continuum. It has a clinic, mobile crisis teams and an emergency room area; its hospital has no inpatient psychiatric unit, and the Department lists no drop-in center o

Volume is reported; results are not. Counts exist for the crisis center, the pediatric unit and the call center. Length of stay, where people came from, where they went next and whether they came back
Grant commitments have no published follow-up. The peer living room, the veterans program and the mobile crisis response targets written into the 2022 grant are on the federal record as promises, and
Start with the federal designation. Cullman County is a mental health professional shortage area for its low-income population, with a score of 16 [52]. Madison County has no area designation at all,

The second measure is the provider ratio, and here two published numbers exist for each county, and a third for Cullman. County Health Rankings' March 2026 figures give 474 residents per mental health

Federal loan repayment is tied to the shortage score of the site where a clinician works, which favors sites in Cullman County; in Madison County only a site with its own facility designation would qu

The official measure gives Madison County no area shortage designation, and a 24-bed unit there could staff six beds a month after opening [52] [56]. The designation was not built to see the kind of s
Nursing is the named bottleneck, and no number describes it. No vacancy or turnover figure for behavioral health nursing was found for WellStone or the hospital system [1] [151].

The pipeline is new and its output is unknown. A psychiatry residency listed two classes in training in October 2026; whether its graduates stay is the question that matters, and none of the program p
No peer training is listed locally, in a region where WellStone's Cullman mobile crisis team was designed in 2020 to pair a clinician with a peer or a case manager [161] [31].

Cullman County's only public transit is a demand-response service [398]. With 37 vehicles, it runs Monday to Friday from 6:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m., and a ride must be scheduled by 2:30 the afternoon befo
The buildings are in one place and the catchment is fifteen counties wide. WellStone has said its Cullman crisis team can take a person to the Huntsville center; beyond that, no source read describes

Record sharing is required and unreported. Whether the crisis center, the hospitals and the courts can see one another's information when a person moves between them is not something any public source

Most of these differences have innocent explanations: different periods, different definitions, a fiscal year against a calendar year. The trouble is that no source says which explanation applies. The

The region is described mostly by people outside it. The figures that can be compared across counties come from national projects and state agencies; the local institutions that hold the operational d
A county split would cost nothing to produce. The Department publishes WellStone's figures without a county split, so no public figure shows how many Cullman residents it serves [64].
Madison County's needs assessment could not be read in full for this report, because the full version is a file of more than 31 megabytes; the smaller county has published one every three years since
The first clinic quality report, when it appears, would be the first published quality and outcome measures for WellStone beyond its access times [173].

geoNotes:
# Map datasets: notes (retrieved 4 October 2026)

The regional maps have two grains. The **fifteen counties** of the Huntsville crisis-center catchment use the county
table checked for the statewide report, unchanged. The **117 census tracts** of Madison and Cullman counties use two
federal sources retrieved for this pack. Everything here was assembled by `build_geo.py` (kept with the draft masters
in `notes/draft/`) from the files in `raw/`.

## What is in the folder

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `ring_counties.csv` | 15 rows: Madison and Cullman (`role` = core) and the thirteen ring counties, with their community mental health center and the 36 county layers of the statewide pack. |
| `alabama_benchmark.csv` | Alabama's value for the same county layers, from the statewide pack's state table. |
| `tracts.csv` | 117 rows, one per census tract: 18 American Community Survey estimates and 10 CDC PLACES estimates, plus the PLACES adult population. |
| `tracts_moe.csv` | The Census Bureau's published margin of error for each of the 18 survey estimates. |
| `benchmarks.csv` | The same 18 survey estimates and margins for Alabama, Madison County and Cullman County, from the same tables. |
| `layers.json` | 65 layer definitions: 36 county layers (`geography: ["county"]`, reference 52) and 29 tract layers (28 map layers and one panel-only denominator; references 406 and 407). |
| `overlays.json` | The core, the crisis catchment, the five community mental health centers, the two 2-1-1 centers, and 54 service locations. |
| `raw/` | The retrieved strings, the check record, the retrieval metadata, the geocoding record and SHA-256 sums. |

## How the tract data was retrieved

The research environment cannot reach census.gov or cdc.gov, so the tract data was fetched in the browser on the
builder's own computer, as the statewide map data was. Each raw file is the compact string built in the browser from
the publisher's own response, typed to disk, and then checked against values computed in the browser before it was
typed: the string's length, a whole-string hash, and for every column the sum and the count of non-empty cells. All
three files matched exactly (`raw/checks.md`). Every tract layer is `retrieval: "browser-js"`.

- **American Community Survey.** The keyed service at api.census.gov now requires an API key and was not used. The
  values come from the endpoint that the data.census.gov table pages themselves call, for tables DP02, DP03, DP04 and
  DP05 of the 2020-2024 five-year release. Variable codes were chosen by their printed labels, which are recorded in
  `raw/retrieval_meta.json`. Percentages are the Bureau's own published percentages (the `PE` variables); nothing was
  computed from counts.
- **Suppressed and not-applicable cells.** One estimate is suppressed: the share of renters paying 35 percent or more
  of income in rent, for Census Tract 106.30 in Madison County (the Bureau prints "-"). Its cell and its margin are
  empty. For Alabama and the two counties, the population total and two percentages are controlled estimates with no
  margin of error (the Bureau prints "*****"); those margin cells are empty and mean "not applicable", not "missing".
- **CDC PLACES.** The 2025 release, GIS-friendly tract file (dataset `yjkw-uj5s`, rows updated 4 December 2025),
  filtered to the two counties: 117 rows, the same tracts as the survey tables. Ten crude-prevalence measures were
  taken. CDC also publishes a 95 percent confidence interval for each value; the intervals were not retrieved, and
  each layer's caveat says so.
- **Tract names** are derived from the tract code (for example `01089010630` is "Census Tract 106.30").

## How to read the two kinds of tract value

The survey values are **sample estimates** with margins of error that are often wide at tract level: a tract's
poverty rate of 20 percent with a margin of 10 points is somewhere between 10 and 30. Show the margin with every
value, and do not rank tracts whose ranges overlap. The PLACES values are **model-based**: CDC predicts each tract
from the statewide health survey and the tract's population mix, so tracts with similar populations get similar
values by construction. They show a pattern across tracts and are not a measurement of any one tract. Neither set of
values is used in the report's text.

## Tract boundaries are not in the pack

The pack carries no geometry. The app fetches the Census Bureau's cartographic boundary file for Alabama's census
tracts when it is built, keeps the 117 tracts of counties 089 and 043, and checks that their identifiers match
`tracts.csv` exactly (the KICKOFF gives the address and the test). The PLACES dataset's own description says its
tract estimates join to the 2023 tract boundary file. County geometry comes from the same package the statewide site
uses.

## Service locations

The 54 locations are places the report names with a street address in a cited source; `ref` on each is the reference
that prints the address. They were placed by geocoding on 4 October 2026, in this order: the Census Bureau's
geocoder (address ranges, current benchmark); where it had no match or matched the wrong street, OpenStreetMap's
Nominatim; and for one campus, the federal treatment locator. `precision` on each point says how far to trust it.

- **`address` (46 points).** The geocoder matched the printed address. Where the source gave no street quadrant
  (Huntsville addresses end in NW, NE, SW or SE) and the geocoder had exactly one match, that match was used and the
  note says so.
- **`approximate` (6 points).** WellStone's Huntsville campus, 4020 and 4040 Memorial Parkway SW, is in neither
  geocoder. Its three markers (the adult crisis center, the pediatric unit and the clinic) use the coordinate that
  SAMHSA's FindTreatment.gov locator gives for WellStone's mental health record at 4040. The locator's substance use
  record for the same address gives a different point, about 1.7 km south, so the position needs a person to confirm
  it. The other approximate points are one HAPPI Health site with two possible quadrants 160 meters apart, the Cullman
  treatment center matched on "Commerce St", and Mountain View Hospital matched on "Scenic Hwy".
- **No marker (2 points).** The Huntsville Vet Center (415 Church Street matches both NW and SW, 900 meters apart)
  and CED's Cherokee County office (no match in either geocoder). They are listed without coordinates.
- A geocoded point is where the address range falls on the street, not the building's front door. Do not present
  the markers as surveyed positions.
- The list is the places the report happens to name with an address. It is not a directory of services, and a tract
  with no marker is not a tract with no services.

## Overlays

- **Crisis catchment** (15 counties) and **community mental health centers** (five centers, one per county) come
  from the Department of Mental Health's pages as read for the statewide report and re-read on 4 October 2026.
  WellStone and Mountain Lakes carry a certified-clinic flag with the month the report gives.
- **2-1-1** lists the counties each of the two centers names on its own page. Seven ring counties are named by
  neither and are left unassigned.
- Not encoded: public health districts, councils of governments, area agencies on aging, homelessness continuums and
  Medicaid regions. The report describes them in prose (Section 13), and the county lists were not all read in a form
  that could be checked row by row.

## Things that need a human eye

- The position of WellStone's Huntsville campus (above).
- County layers are a year or more older than some tract layers and use different definitions (QuickFacts "persons
  in poverty" against the survey's five-year poverty rate, for example). Do not put a county value and a tract value
  in the same sentence without their vintages.
- Small renter counts make several tract housing figures unstable: margins of 40 to 88 points appear for the
  rent-burden layer in `tracts_moe.csv`.
